references.text: God predicts that in seven days He will cause it to rain over the earth—the seven days referred to in Gen 7:10 as completed before the flood came.
Describes how the flood came upon the earth for forty days, a direct continuation of the waters coming after the seven waiting days.
The only place outside Genesis where the Hebrew word 'mabbul' (flood) is used: 'The Lord sat enthroned over the flood'—a clear reference to the great deluge.
By faith Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, built an ark to save his household—a testimony to Noah's faith during the waiting period before the flood came.
Points to God's patience in Noah's days while the ark was being built, and how eight souls were saved through water—a parallel to the waiting days before the flood.
God did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah and seven others when He brought the flood upon the world of the ungodly.
Literary and theological parallel: 'Seven days' as a divine waiting period before new revelation or action.
